chapterTitle: Employee Stock Options (ESOs): Mechanics, Vesting, Dilution, Backdating Scandals, and Hull-White Valuation

scenes.title: The Unique Structure of Employee Stock Options

beatOutlines.textOutline: A corporate finance student asks how employee stock options differ from listed exchange options; the mentor highlights non-transferability and 10-year maturities ([fact-01]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: They examine vesting mechanisms: cliff vesting (100% at once) versus graded vesting (incremental annual tranches) ([fact-02]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The mentor discusses the moral hazard of asymmetric payoffs, where managers enjoy unlimited upside but zero downside, encouraging high-variance gambles ([fact-03]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: ESO Valuation & Overstatement Metrics by the Numbers

beatOutlines.textOutline: Display standard 10-year Black-Scholes valuation: $25.96 per share ($2,596 per 100-share contract) for an at-the-money ESO with S0 = $50 and sigma = 30% ([fact-08]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Display Hull-White model valuation: incorporating early exercise multiple M = 1.5 ($75 threshold) and forfeiture rate lambda = 4% drops fair value to $18.60 per share, proving BSM overstates costs by over 39% ([fact-08]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Cliff Vesting vs. Graded Vesting Mechanisms

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare Cliff Vesting: 100% of options vest simultaneously at a single future date (e.g., exactly 3 years post-grant); departing early forfeits everything ([fact-01], [fact-02]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare Graded Vesting: equal tranches vest incrementally over consecutive years (e.g., 25% vesting annually across 4 years) ([fact-02]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Break down Early Exercise Boundary: at any node after t_vest, if stock price S >= M * K (e.g., $75), employee exercises immediately ([fact-07]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Break down Forfeiture Adjustment: constant annual departure rate lambda applied across binomial tree steps to capture employee turnover ([fact-07]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Business Snapshot 14.1: Share Dilution & EPS Impact

beatOutlines.textOutline: Examine Exchange-Traded Option Settlement: settled with existing shares in secondary markets without altering corporate share counts ([fact-05]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Examine ESO Exercise Dilution: issuing newly minted shares expands total outstanding share base, directly diluting future Earnings Per Share (EPS) unless offset by share repurchases ([fact-05]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Standard BSM Overvaluation vs. Hull-White Realism

beatOutlines.textOutline: Balance Standard BSM: assumes holding to 10-year maturity and unlimited risk tolerance, producing inflated values like $25.96 ([fact-08]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Balance Hull-White Realism: reflects executive risk aversion and early exercise at multiple M, reducing fair value to $18.60 and correcting 39% overstatement ([fact-07], [fact-08], [fact-10]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Employee Terminal Gross Payoff vs. Corporate Treasury Net Cost

beatOutlines.textOutline: Plot Employee Gross Cash Payoff: max(S_T - K, 0) upon exercise with $0.00 out-of-pocket cash premium paid ([fact-09]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Plot Corporate Treasury Perspective: Net economic cost equals payoff minus amortized grant-date fair market value per share ([fact-09]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Option Backdating (Lie 2005): retroactively selecting historical grant dates when stock prices were at cyclic lows to give executives instant in-the-money value unrecorded as expense ([fact-06]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Spring Loading & Post-Termination Windows: granting options right before positive announcements, and enforcing 60-90 day post-resignation exercise limits ([fact-06], [fact-11]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

summarySteps: 1. ESO Structure ([fact-01]): Non-transferable call options granted with up to 10-year maturities, requiring vesting and forfeiting upon departure.
2. Vesting Mechanisms ([fact-02]): Cliff vesting (100% at once) and graded vesting (incremental annual tranches across years).
3. Moral Hazard ([fact-03]): Asymmetric call payoffs incentivize executives to take excessive leverage and high-variance corporate gambles.
4. Accounting Expensing ([fact-04]): FAS 123R (ASC 718) and IFRS 2 mandate grant-date fair value expensing amortized pro-rata over vesting.
5. Share Dilution ([fact-05]): ESO exercises require newly minted common stock, expanding share counts and diluting future Earnings Per Share (EPS).
6. Backdating Scandals ([fact-06]): Erik Lie (2005) exposed retroactive backdating to cyclic stock lows and spring loading before positive announcements.
7. Hull-White Valuation ([fact-07]): Incorporates early exercise multiple M (S >= M*K) and employee forfeiture rates lambda into binomial trees.
8. BSM Overstatement Correction ([fact-08]): Hull-White valuation reduces ESO fair value from $25.96 (BSM) to $18.60, correcting a 39% overstatement due to early exercise.
bottomTakeaway: Employee stock options require specialized binomial valuation models like Hull-White to account for early exercise and forfeiture, correcting standard Black-Scholes overstatements while managing accounting expensing and EPS dilution ([fact-01], [fact-04], [fact-05], [fact-07], [fact-08]).
